title: Cap. VIII: Mode likeness denied — Calvin's two Adam–Christ differences
pass_a_gloss: As to the minor: Placeus has already often denied that the likeness of mode must be pressed — the mode by which we have condemnation from Adam and justification from Christ. He has confirmed this by great men's authority and by examples. Hear Calvin if you will: it is worth marking two differences here between Christ and Adam; the Apostle did not skip them as negligible, but because listing them did not serve the present argument. First: we are not damned by Adam's sin through imputation alone, as if another's sin's penalty were exacted from us; we bear his penalty because we are also guilty of fault, inasmuch as our nature corrupted in him is bound before God under iniquity's guilt. But by Christ's righteousness we are restored to salvation another way: it is not credited to us because it is inside us, but because by the Father's bounty we possess Christ himself with all his goods. So the gift of righteousness does not mean a quality God pours into us (as some wrongly take it) but the free imputation of righteousness.
pass_b_english: But as to the minor: we have already denied several times that the likeness must be pressed in the mode by which we have condemnation from Adam and justification from Christ. And we have confirmed this both by the authority of great men and by several examples. Hear Calvin, if you please: "Further, it is worth noting here two differences between Christ and Adam: which the Apostle did not omit because he judged them negligible, but because it did not serve the present argument to enumerate them. The first is that we are not damned by Adam's sin through imputation alone, as if the penalty of another's sin were being exacted from us: but we therefore bear his penalty because we are also guilty of the fault, inasmuch as our nature, corrupted in him, is bound before God under the guilt of iniquity. But by Christ's righteousness we are restored to salvation in another way: for it is not therefore credited to us because it is within us, but because we possess Christ himself with all his goods, given to us by the Father's bounty. And so the gift of righteousness signifies not a quality with which God imbues us, as some wrongly interpret, but the free imputation of righteousness."
source_text: Ad minorem autem quod spectat, jam aliquoties negavimus urgeri debere similitudinem in modo, quo ab Adamo condemnationem, & a Christo iustificationem habemus. Idque cum autoritate magnorum virorum, tum aliquot exemplis comprobavimus. Audi, si placet, Calvinum, Porro duas hic differentias inter Christum & Adamum notare operae pretium est: quas non ideo praeteriit Apostolus, quia negligendas censeret, sed quia praesentis argumenti nihil referebat eas enumerare. Prior est quod peccato Adae non per solam imputationem damnamur, ac si alieni peccati exigeretur a nobis poena: sed ideo poenam eius sustinemus, quia & culpae sumus rei, quatenus scilicet natura nostra in ipso vitiata, iniquitatis reatu astringitur apud Deum. At per Christi iustitiam alio modo in salutem restituimur: neque enim ideo nobis accepta fertur, quia intra nos sit: sed quod Christum ipsum cum bonis suis omnibus, Patris largitate nobis donatum possidemus. Itaque donum iustitiae, non qualitatem qua nos Deus imbuat, ut perperam quidam interpretantur, sed gratuitam iustitiae imputationem significat.
